strengths: Systematic and thorough diagnostic analysis revealing LLM limitations in long-horizon planning (50-65% full-procedure alignment vs. 75-86% next-state), providing clear motivation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two benchmarks with multiple LLM backbones, consistent improvements of 7.2-25.3%, and extensive ablations (oracle grounding, horizons, retrieval strategies)
Well-designed probing tasks that are more systematic than prior work and provide clear evidence of performance degradation over planning horizons
Detailed reproducibility support including action spaces, prompts, tutorial sources, and cost analysis enabling future research
Clear presentation of framework and methodology with well-illustrated figures and algorithmic descriptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: retrieval-augmentation, LongCoT, and listwise reward estimation are all from prior work; primary contribution is engineering their combination rather than introducing fundamentally new methods

Significant practical limitations that reduce generalizability: requires tutorial availability (acknowledged as bottleneck), manual annotation of 1-2 relevant tutorial chunks per task (198 annotations) with no inter-rater agreement reported, and only 33% and 14% of benchmark tasks evaluated due to tutorial availability constraints

Weak baseline comparison: WoM baseline is a modified variant of WebDreamer using LongCoT rather than original iterative rollouts, making it unclear whether improvements come from R-WoM or LongCoT; original WebDreamer excluded on efficiency grounds but cost data provided suggests fair comparison was possible

Highly variable domain-dependent improvements (Table 4): minimal gains for VLC (0.67-1%), VS Code (0-0.67%), but large gains elsewhere; unexplained variance suggests method benefits are not general-purpose

Insufficient retrieval quality analysis: Figure 8 shows low Recall@1 (~49% for WebArena with both strategies); large gap between R-WoM and oracle grounding (Figure 3) indicates retrieval is major bottleneck; limited investigation of failure modes or which tutorial knowledge helps most

Significant computational overhead remains despite efficiency gains over iterative rollouts: ~5x more LLM calls than vanilla approaches (~11,515 vs. 2,028 for Qwen), ~12 hours vs. ~2 hours for OSWorld, limiting practical applicability

Methodological concerns with probing tasks: small sample sizes (40-100 samples), full-procedure alignment uses tutorials that are also used in R-WoM introducing potential circularity, and LLM judge evaluation for procedure alignment could have built-in biases

Limited technical depth: Equation 11 (listwise reward) described as novel but is essentially comparative scoring; limited explanation of LongCoT adaptation from Deepseek-R1; minimal ablations on individual component contributions

Missing error analysis and failure cases: no detailed investigation of when/why improvements help, why benefits plateau at horizon 3, or why improvements vary dramatically between models (Qwen vs. Claude)

Generalization concerns: only evaluated on digital agent tasks with tutorial availability, subset-based task selection (85/256 and 113/812 benchmarks), unclear applicability to tutorial-scarce domains or other task types

strengths: Systematic and well-designed probing study (Section 3) that provides valuable empirical insights into LLM world modeling limitations across short-term (>75% accuracy) and long-horizon (≤65%) planning horizons

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two benchmarks with multiple model backbones, multiple runs with standard deviations, and thoughtful ablations on grounding levels and imagination horizons
Consistent empirical improvements of 7.2-25.3% across models and benchmarks, with particularly large gains in long-horizon tasks (e.g., GIMP +60%, Chrome +60%)
Clear presentation with effective motivation (Figure 1) and detailed appendix providing implementation transparency including prompts, additional experiments, and domain-level analysis
Thorough exploration of design components including query rewriting, reranking, and LongCoT reasoning with ablations demonstrating their complementary effects
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is applying standard RAG to world models; retrieval-augmented LLM generation and tutorial-guided agent grounding are established techniques with similar ideas explored concurrently (AgentTrek, TongUI, Learn-by-interact) without empirical comparison

Severe task filtering introduces critical scope limitations and selection bias: Only 85/365 (~23%) OSWorld and 113/812 (~14%) WebArena tasks have tutorials; generalizability to full benchmarks unclear and tasks without tutorials likely have different characteristics
Large oracle-retrieval gap in Figure 3 (3-6% absolute) indicates retrieval quality is a substantial bottleneck, questioning practical applicability; this critical issue deserves more discussion

Missing critical ablations: Listwise vs. absolute reward estimation not directly compared despite being claimed as contribution; query rewriting/reranking ablations relegated to appendix; number of retrieved chunks (top-5) not justified
Computational cost inadequately addressed: Table 5 shows ~6x overhead (12h vs 2h on OSWorld), a major practical limitation relegated to appendix with only vague future work on 'agentic calling'

Methodological concerns: LLM judge evaluation uses Claude-3.7-Sonnet for both generation and evaluation in plan alignment task, risking systematic bias; WoM baseline uses different rollout strategy than original WebDreamer, confounding interpretation

Shallow mechanistic understanding: Paper demonstrates that grounding helps but provides limited insight into why; no analysis of which tutorial information is used, which task types benefit most, or failure modes

Probing task limitations: Small sample sizes (100 next-state, 40 plan alignment, 98 milestone); lexically similar distractors may not capture realistic confusions; unknown correlation between isolated probing tasks and end-to-end performance

Limited applicability: Requirement for high-quality, up-to-date tutorials acknowledged in conclusion but not addressed; no investigation of robustness to outdated/incorrect/low-quality tutorials or tutorial-scarce domains

strengths: Systematic probing analysis that clearly identifies LLM limitations in long-horizon world modeling through three well-designed evaluation tasks with results showing sharp performance degradation (50-65% on full-procedure planning vs. >75% on next-state identification)
Consistent empirical improvements across multiple models (Qwen-2.5-VL-72B, Claude-3.5/3.7-Sonnet) and benchmarks (OSWorld, WebArena), with gains of 7.2-25.3% depending on setting
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple baselines (Vanilla, RAG, WoM), ablation studies on imagination horizon showing sustained grounding benefits, and retrieval strategy ablations
Clear demonstration that grounding principle works through oracle tutorial experiments (Figure 3) showing progressive improvement from no grounding → retrieved → oracle tutorials
Thorough reproducibility support with extensive implementation details, prompts in appendix, tutorial sources, and cost analysis across configurations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—core components are combinations of existing techniques: query rewriting and LLM-based reranking (standard RAG), LongCoT reasoning (Deepseek-R1 inspired), and listwise ranking (adapted from recent preference optimization work). No novel insights specific to world modeling

Critical practical limitation: approach requires tutorial availability; only evaluated on task subsets where tutorials exist with large performance gaps between retrieved and oracle tutorials (Figure 3), severely restricting applicability to undocumented domains

Missing component-level ablations for R-WoM design choices—no isolated analysis of query rewriting, LLM reranking, LongCoT rollout, or listwise ranking contributions, making it unclear which components drive improvements

Comparison fairness concerns: WoM reimplemented as LongCoT variant rather than using original iterative approach, and OSWorld uses auxiliary GTA-1-7B action grounding model, making direct comparison problematic and conflating implementation choices with method novelty

Incomplete analysis of results: no qualitative failure case examination, no explanation for highly variable domain-level performance (VLC gains ~0.3-0.7 vs. GIMP ~1-5), no statistical significance testing despite overlapping error bars, and no cost-benefit analysis (R-WoM uses 5-6x more LLM calls than baselines)

Probing task limitations: full-procedure alignment relies on subjective manual annotation of reference procedures with only 'one or two chunks' per task and unreported inter-annotator agreement; LLM judge introduces additional variance

Incomplete reward estimation evaluation: milestone transition recognition only tests ranking of good vs. bad trajectories, not whether scores correlate with actual task success, and lacks justification for why listwise ranking should provide claimed 'more robust and consistent action selection'

Limited long-horizon analysis: Figure 4 shows performance plateaus around horizon 3, suggesting fundamental limitations persist even with grounding; no investigation of how retrieval specifically mitigates error compounding in extended rollouts

strengths: Systematic and well-motivated probing analysis (Section 3) that clearly reveals LLM limitations in long-horizon planning while showing competence in short-term reasoning

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple LLM backbones with consistent improvements (5.6-23.4%) and extensive ablation studies examining retrieval quality, imagination horizons, and cost-performance tradeoffs
Practical framework design with thoughtful optimizations: LongCoT for efficiency, adaptive branching/deduplication to reduce costs by 50%+ while retaining most performance gains

Honest failure analysis providing insights into when the method works (information-seeking: 19-37% failure) vs. fails (content-modification: 65-80% failure), with discussion of retrieval failure modes
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (RAG, LongCoT, listwise ranking) without introducing fundamentally new methods or insights for world modeling
Severely constrained evaluation scope: only ~24% of OSWorld and 38% of WebArena tasks have available tutorials, substantially limiting the generalizability and real-world applicability of results

Unclear methodological contributions: gap between oracle retrieval performance (40-41%) and actual retrieval (31-40%) in Figure 4 suggests retrieval is a significant bottleneck not fully addressed; ablations don't cleanly isolate contributions of retrieval vs. LongCoT vs. listwise ranking

Significant performance variance across models (Qwen: 37%, Claude-3.5: 26%, Claude-3.7: 38% on OSWorld) that often exceeds method improvements, and unexplained differences between WebArena (5.6-16.3% gains) and OSWorld (10.8-23.4%) performance gains
Systematic failure modes on content-modification tasks (65-80% failure rate) with limited proposed solutions; brittleness suggested by reliance on heuristic filtering when retrieval fails

Missing important ablations: no comparison of different retrieval recall thresholds, limited evaluation of synthesized tutorials (Section 5.5 shows only 3-4% absolute improvement), and lack of statistical significance testing

strengths: Well-designed probing analysis revealing clear degradation of LLM world models from short-horizon (77-86%) to long-horizon (50-65%) tasks
Systematic and comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple LLMs, two benchmarks, and various ablations with detailed appendix
Intuitive approach combining query rewriting, reranking, and listwise reward ranking with clear motivations
Consistent improvements across three different LLMs (Qwen-2.5-VL, Claude-3.5, Claude-3.7) suggesting generalizability
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: RAG for agents, LongCoT rollouts (from DeepSeek-R1), and listwise reward ranking are all from prior work; the contribution is primarily their combination in this context

Evaluation on task subsets where tutorials exist (87/361 OSWorld, 113/301 WebArena) rather than full benchmarks—improvements of 23.4% and 16.3% only apply to 24-38% of tasks; full-benchmark gains would be much smaller
Tutorial availability is a fundamental practical constraint affecting ~60-75% of tasks, but is not adequately discussed as a core limitation upfront
Weak baseline comparisons: unclear if all methods use the same auxiliary action grounding model (GTA-1-7B); WebDreamer and Vanilla baselines may not be fairly reimplemented in identical settings
Modest empirical gains on full benchmarks (5.6% WebArena improvement for best model) do not justify added complexity; unclear which components (retrieval, LongCoT, listwise reward) drive improvements

Probing evaluation concerns: LLM judges show inconsistency across models (Table 12: 65% vs 60% vs 65%); negative sample construction via difflib oversimplified; only single reference procedure per task
Insufficient failure mode analysis: Table 11 shows content-modification tasks fail 76-80% of the time, but paper offers no concrete solutions, only vague suggestions about 'richer strategies'
No statistical significance testing despite modest improvements and limited sample sizes (~87 tasks); ablation of candidate number (Table 15) and other hyperparameters appears post-hoc
High computational costs (410-989s per task) with no cost-benefit analysis; unclear when 5-6% improvements justify 10+ minutes of inference
Section 5.5 on tutorial-scarce settings shows only 3.4-6.0% improvements, suggesting tutorial synthesis is limited; core methodological assumption (tutorial availability) is severely constraining

strengths: Clear and systematic problem diagnosis via three well-designed probing tasks that clearly demonstrate LLM limitations in long-horizon reasoning (86% next-state vs. 65% full-procedure)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with consistent 5.6%-23.4% improvements across multiple benchmarks, models, and settings, including honest failure analysis
Practical framework design with well-justified choices (listwise rewards, adaptive branching) that reduce computational cost by 50% while maintaining performance
Strong empirical validation showing monotonic improvement with grounding quality (Figure 4) and sustained performance over longer horizons (Figure 5)
Thorough implementation details, extensive ablations (RQ1-RQ4), and transparent cost-performance analysis demonstrating methodological rigor
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: query rewriting + reranking is standard RAG, LongCoT rollouts are inspired by existing work, listwise rewards draw from concurrent literature - contribution is primarily in problem diagnosis and system combination

Fundamental practical limitations: only 24% OSWorld and 38% WebArena tasks have tutorial coverage, limiting real-world applicability; no solution proposed for 62-80% failure rate on content-modification tasks

Evaluation concerns: full-procedure alignment relies on manual annotation of 40 procedures with LLM judges (potential bias), probing analysis uses small samples (40-100) without error bars, no human validation of judge decisions

Incomplete analysis of failure modes: paper identifies failures in implicit reasoning tasks but provides no mechanism to determine when grounding helps vs. hurts; tutorial quality dependency not explored
Cost remains challenging: full R-WoM requires 2-4x token budget vs. vanilla; adaptive variant sacrifices 1-2% performance (Table 6); practical viability for large-scale deployment unclear
